P0_mechanism_freeze.frozen_name: Rate-Limited Physiologic Conductance Control for Multi-Segment CSF Drainage
P0_mechanism_freeze.central_claim: Bounded-rate conductance slew (2%/sec) + multi-segment continuous redistribution
P0_mechanism_freeze.sensor_health_fallback: Demoted to implementation module (NOT central claim) because US20260115436A1 already covers sensor-failure handling

P2_prototype_BOM.total_cost: $7,000-10,000 (all COTS, no custom fab except acrylic manifold)

P3_TTP_upgrade.structure: 3 boxes on page one: What is Known (225-run ablation, 180-run comparison, provenance, prior art) / What is Hypothesized (physical bench reproduces 2-3x, economic value) / What Buyer Can Test (80-run blinded protocol, primary endpoint, falsification criteria)
P3_TTP_upgrade.commercial_argument: Existing tech provides closed-loop/fallback/flow regulation. Our contribution: bounded-rate multi-segment conductance regime producing measurable robustness advantage.

P1_bench_protocol.status: READY from R284, now with confirmed mechanism and primary endpoint
P1_bench_protocol.primary_endpoint: Time-to-critical hydraulic state under sensor uncertainty (NOT '2.7x')
P1_bench_protocol.design_principle: Designed to DISPROVE the computational result. If bench disagrees with simulator by >30%, simulator is wrong.

P4_buyer_outreach.message: We developed a bounded-rate conductance-control approach for multi-segment CSF drainage. In our 225-run ablation the rate-limiting mechanism is the dominant contributor to the simulated advantage. We have a blinded physical protocol designed specifically to falsify the computational result. We'd like your engineering team to try to break it.
P4_buyer_outreach.framing: Technical evaluation, not transaction. Buyer's objections become machine-readable evidence.
